title: Scaled-Cayley Mirror recurrent dynamics
hypothesis: A shared orthogonal recurrent transition plus a compact skew-symmetric Cayley coordinate will represent multiple stable task dynamics at lower serialized bytes than independent task-specific orthogonal matrices, while preserving multi-step rollout quality. Larger angle tasks may expose the limited coordinate subspace.
physical_object: shared base orthogonal recurrent transition matrix
mirror_coordinate: two coefficients over shared skew-symmetric generators, composed through a Cayley map
controls: tied shared orthogonal transition with no task code
shared transition plus rank-2 skew-Cayley Mirror code
task-specific full orthogonal transition upper control
shared transition plus unconstrained rank-2 additive residual
task: Synthetic 4D linear recurrence; fit task dynamics from support state transitions, evaluate multi-step rollout MSE and spectral stability on held-out initial states.

development.selection_metric: Fit four fixed development task transitions to estimate the shared transition/generator span and choose only scalar normalization; fit task coordinates with frozen rank 2. No fresh data used for method selection.

fresh.split: Four development task matrices determine the shared base/generator span; each fresh world includes 6 low-angle and 6 high-angle task dynamics, 128 support transitions and 32 held-out 32-step trajectories per task.

success_gate: On >=2/3 fresh worlds, low-angle Mirror 32-step MSE <=1.05x full orthogonal control, spectral radius <=1.001, and actual payload <=60% of task-specific matrices. Report high-angle boundary and Cayley solve overhead.
failure_gate: FAIL if low-angle rollout or stability gate fails on >=2/3 worlds, or payload exceeds 60% without a quality advantage over tied shared control. PROMISING is scoped recurrence evidence only; no general RNN claim.
boundaries: teacher dynamics are generated from a low-rank Cayley family
no language or long-horizon real sequence task
Cayley orthogonality does not imply useful task diversity
